texts.preamble: Vaishnavi Sanjay Potdukhe vs Santhosha.R on 15 November, 2024 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.1356/2023 Kabc0B0002802023 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 15th Day of November-2024 M.V.C. No.1356/2023 Petitioner/s: 1. Vaishnavi Sanjay Potdukhe, D/o SanjauPotdukhe, Aged about 24 years, Permanent Resident of Plot No.655, Devashish, Umrer Road, Behind Panchavati Vruddhashram, Chitnis Nagar, Ayodha Nagar, Nagpur, Maharashtra-440024. (By Sri. M. Subramani, Adv.,) Vs. Respondent/s: 1. Santhosha. R S/o Munirajappa. B, Seegehalli Village, Kannamangala Post, Bangalore.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 16.01.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 16.01.2023 at about 9.30 a.m., petitioner was riding Scooter bearing Reg. No. MH-49-W- 8607 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Seegehalli-Kadugodi Road, at that time one Tractor & Trailer bearing Reg. No. KA-07-T-0604 & KA-07-T-0605 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner. Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately, he was shifted to Axis Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 24 years, the petitioner was working as Software Engineer and earning Rs.35,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost her future income. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court and hence placed exparte. Vaishnavi Sanjay Potdukhe vs Santhosha.R on 15 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124021836/ 2 The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 170, 134(c) and 158(6) of M. V. Act. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The respondent No.1 further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.21 and examined one Shahid Parveez, Billing Supervisor at Manipal Hospital as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.22 and Ex.P.23 and examined Anil Ramesh as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.24 and 25 and also examined Dr. Deepu N.K as PW.4 and got marked the document at Ex.P26 and closed their side. On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
texts.arguments: 17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 18. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was Software Engineer at MU Sigma Company, ITPL, Bangalore and earning Rs.35,000/- per month, but no reliable evidence is produced by the petitioner to show how much income she was getting from her work. But during the course of cross-examination, the petitioner admitted that, she is still working in MU Sigma business solution Company Pvt. Ltd., as Data Analyst and earning sum of Rs.50,000/- per month, that means the petitioner is continued in service and accidental injuries has not caused any permanent disability. Hence, petitioner is not entitled for loss of future earning capacity on account of disability. 24. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES: Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 16.01.2023 to 26.01.2023 i.e., 10 days. Further, the petitioner submitted that her parents came from Nagpur by flight and spent huge amount for the same and produced the flight tickets and boarding pass which are marked at Ex.P.20 and Ex.P.21, for Rs.28,732/-. Hence, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.58,732/- under the head of nutritious food, conveyance and attendant charges. 25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS AS WELL AS MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS : The petitioner was aged about 24 years at the time of accident, she has sustained grievous injuries. It shows that she found difficulty in doing day to day works. She might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life. During the course of argument, learned counsel for petitioner argued that due to injury marriage prospectus of petitioner have been diminished. Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness as well as marriage prospectus. 26. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES : The petitioner has claimed Rs.6,26,000/- towards future medical expenses. The doctor who has been examined as PW.4 has suggested future surgeries for Right axillary contracture and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.1,86,000/-, Breast contracture and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.2,00,000/- and expander removal and multiple advancement flaps and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.2,40,000/-. By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as she is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital. Hence, under this head Rs.3,00,000/- is awarded. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads: 1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/- 2 Medical expenses Rs. 1,29,964/- 3 Loss of earnings during laid Rs. 32,000/- up period 4 As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
